name: opensc
desc: Tools and libraries for smart cards
why: Smart card tooling opens a real door into APDU traffic and card file structures, though it is fairly standard infrastructure.

brief.what_it_is: OpenSC is a set of libraries and command-line utilities for working with smart cards, with its main focus on cards that support cryptographic operations. The wiki says it implements the standard smart card APIs (PKCS#11, Windows Smart Card Minidriver, and macOS CryptoTokenKit) so applications can use those cards. The brew formula installs about two dozen tools, including pkcs11-tool, pkcs15-tool, opensc-tool, opensc-explorer, and piv-tool. The fetched pages did not show the exact inputs and outputs of each tool.
brief.why_it_exists: The wiki frames it as serving security applications such as authentication, mail encryption and digital signatures, by making smart cards usable through standard APIs. It is written by an international team of volunteers and licensed as open source.
brief.how_it_works: Neither the wiki nor the README explains the internals in detail. The wiki says OpenSC implements the standard APIs so that applications can reach cards through them. Related sub-projects such as libp11 and pkcs11-helper are wrapper libraries for PKCS#11 modules, and they can be used without OpenSC.
brief.install_notes: The brew caveat says the OpenSSH PKCS11 smartcard integration will not work with this formula. To get that functionality, unlink this formula and install the OpenSC cask instead. The README lists official downloads: Windows MSI installers for x64, x86 and arm64, a macOS DMG, and a source tarball for Unix. Unix build steps are on the wiki page 'Compiling and Installing on Unix flavors', and there are Windows and macOS Quick Start pages. Nightly builds are available by git hash from the OpenSC/Nightly repo. The wiki says download links should come from the README or the GitHub main page, not the wiki. I did not see reader hardware or first-run configuration requirements in the pages I read.
brief.standout: OpenSC is a family rather than one tool. It implements several platform smart-card APIs at once and ships sub-projects (libp11, pkcs11-helper, PAM-PKCS#11, pam_p11, OpenCT, OpenSC-Java) that can be used independently. The README also lists a card support matrix covering CAC, SmartCard-HSM, PIV, OpenPGP, GIDS, and Pico HSM applets, with CI, Coverity, CodeQL, and OSS-Fuzz badges. The security history is tied to APDU and response data handling, which fits the scout note about APDU traffic and card file structures.
brief.status: maintained. The wiki news lists OpenSC 0.27.0 as available on 30.03.2026, with a security advisory posted the same day. The GitHub page says the wiki Home was last edited Nov 27, 2025. The README shows live CI badges. I did not check the commit log directly.
brief.caveats: The brew formula does not support OpenSSH PKCS11 smartcard integration (see the install notes). Several security advisories cover data handling issues before 0.27.0 (CVE-2025-49010, CVE-2025-66037, CVE-2025-66038, CVE-2025-13763, CVE-2025-66215), so older versions are a concern. The wiki no longer accepts public edits because of spam, and changes go through pull requests to OpenSC/Wiki. The license is LGPL 2.1 or later. The README contains no command examples, and the tools manual link failed to load, so I did not verify what each tool does beyond its name.
quotes: OpenSC provides a set of libraries and utilities to work with smart cards.
Its main focus is on cards that support cryptographic operations, and facilitate their use in security applications such as authentication, mail encryption and digital signatures.
Manual pages for the OpenSC command line tools are available online and typically distributed along with your installation.
